Media.net interview experience
Oh boy, where do I even begin? I had the most delightful interview experience of my life — and by delightful, I mean a complete disaster that could’ve been a parody skit.

So this was the grand finale: a final round with the VP of Engineering at media.net. Big title, right? Except this guy was multitasking like a true champion. Half the time he was talking on the phone, occasionally gracing me with some thoughtful chewing sounds of his sandwich and sprinkling in a few burps here and there — because, you know, professionalism. At one point I genuinely thought I had accidentally joined a kitchen staff meeting at a local dhaba.

Between mouthfuls and random side conversations with people around him, he’d randomly scream, “I don’t understand your solution!” — shocking, considering he wasn’t even listening in the first place. Maybe next time I’ll just mime the answer while he’s busy with his lunch and family reunion happening in the background.

Then came the cherry on top: he wanted me to design LinkedIn. Okay, cool. But wait — with exact numbers for total users and daily active users. Because apparently, I moonlight as a LinkedIn data engineer when I’m not applying for jobs. I threw out a ballpark of 100 million (you know, just trying to move things along), and this guy starts taunting and shouting like I personally offended the sacred LinkedIn analytics god.

Honestly, it felt less like an interview and more like he was working out some unresolved rage from a fight he had five minutes earlier. Or maybe every interview is just his personal anger
